correctness.rationale: Derivation from the normalized modified-Helmholtz Robin BVP gives the unique closed-form surface-before-bulk transform. The objective derivative has positive denominator and quadratic numerator P(a). For starts closer to the left, P is strictly decreasing because Z−delta*K*sinh(k)=sinh(k)*H+K*B2>0; P(K)=delta*sinh(k)−B1*K−B2*K^2 changes sign at one explicit positive Kc. The midpoint and reflected domains are covered separately and the equality at Kc is included. Independent tridiagonal finite-difference checks (100 sets), scalar maximization (100 sets), and threshold tests all passed. Such testing supports but does not replace the global analytic proof.

value.rationale: When a target particle may be lost in the bulk, distributing fixed surface catalytic reactivity to maximize capture is a naturally motivated resource allocation problem. The sharp allocation switch from a single nearer active endpoint to a unique interior split is a nontrivial qualitative effect missing in the known same-geometry mean-time optimum. The all-parameter threshold and the exact boundary-start physical scale support reproducible design comparisons; no downstream theorem or experimental deployment is claimed.
